item.title: Putin’s Ukraine War Is Killing Russia’s Poorest
item.description: Russia’s intentional avoidance of deploying residents of large urban centers is aimed at preventing political instability. The post Putin’s Ukraine War Is Killing Russia’s Poorest appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: In 1944, Three Americans and Four Germans Spent Christmas Together in Hell
item.description: A German mother sheltered three lost American soldiers during the Battle of the Bulge—and did the same for German soldiers hours later. The post In 1944, Three Americans and Four Germans Spent Christmas Together in Hell appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Fall of Hong Kong Was a “Black Christmas” for the British Empire
item.description: The defenders of Hong Kong, tens of thousands of miles from any conceivable relief force, surrendered the territory to Imperial Japan on December 25, 1941. The post The Fall of Hong Kong Was a “Black Christmas” for the British Empire appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: From Flip Phone to iPhone: The Arleigh-Burke Destroyer Gets a Radar Leap
item.description: The Arleigh Burke-class destroyers, which can conduct anti-surface warfare, anti-submarine warfare, and air defense operations, are the cornerstone of the Navy’s surface combatant fleet. The post From Flip Phone to iPhone: The Arleigh-Burke Destroyer Gets a Radar Leap appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Did Nixon Order a “Christmas Bombing” of North Vietnam in 1972? Not Exactly
item.description: Though Nixon initiated Operation Linebacker II, a bombing campaign against North Vietnam coinciding with the Christmas holiday, he suspended bombing operations on Christmas Day for humanitarian reasons. The post Did Nixon Order a “Christmas Bombing” of North Vietnam in 1972? Not Exactly appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: America’s Deadliest Fighter Was Built at the Wrong Time
item.description: It wasn’t until September 2014 that an F-22 Raptor even took part in combat, carrying out an airstrike on ISIS positions in Syria. The post America’s Deadliest Fighter Was Built at the Wrong Time appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Christmas “Raid on Cuxhaven” Was the First Carrier Raid in History
item.description: The raid was not militarily significant—but it was proof that planes could take off from ships and attack land targets, giving them a new significance in naval operations. The post The Christmas “Raid on Cuxhaven” Was the First Carrier Raid in History appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Christmas 1940 Under Siege: Admiral Hipper and the Battle for the Atlantic
item.description: In a narrow sense, the Admiral Hipper “won” the naval battle; it inflicted damage on the British convoy and escaped to fight another day. But it failed to destroy it. item.title: Japan’s Development Pitch to Central Asia
item.description: By announcing new investments in Central Asia, Japan is entering a crowded field of competition and must prove the advantages of cooperation with it. The post Japan’s Development Pitch to Central Asia appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why the Gaza Governance Plan Can’t Wait
item.description: President Donald Trump has the chance to begin the reconstruction of the Gaza Strip. Delay will only destabilize the situation. The post Why the Gaza Governance Plan Can’t Wait appeared first on The National Interest.
